chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from a man, from Jameel, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The believers are servants to one another.' I said: 'And how can they be servants to one another?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'One benefits the other through the Hadith.'
ai.seo_question: How do believers serve each other according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) redefines the concept of servitude among believers not as hierarchy, but as mutual intellectual service, where the primary mode of assistance is the transmission and sharing of religious knowledge (Hadith). This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the communal responsibility of preserving and disseminating divine wisdom, transforming the believer into a conduit for spiritual and intellectual enrichment of the community.
